short_definition: A comprehensive European Union law regulating data privacy and personal data protection.
layman_explanation: A strict set of European laws giving individuals control over how companies collect and use their personal data.

short_definition: California data privacy legislation granting consumers rights regarding their personal information.
layman_explanation: Laws in California giving residents the right to know what personal data companies sell and the right to opt out.

short_definition: Any data that could potentially identify a specific individual directly or indirectly.
layman_explanation: Details like your Social Security number, home address, full name, or fingerprint that reveal who you are.

short_definition: Demographic information, medical histories, test results, and insurance data protected under healthcare laws.
layman_explanation: Your private medical records, doctor visit history, and prescription details.

short_definition: U.S. law providing privacy standards to protect patients' medical records and health information.
layman_explanation: Rules that prevent doctors, hospitals, and medical apps from sharing your health details without permission.

short_definition: Tools and policies designed to ensure sensitive data is not lost, misused, or accessed by unauthorized users.
layman_explanation: Security software blocking employees from accidentally emailing sensitive customer lists outside the firm.

short_definition: The principle of collecting only the personal data strictly necessary to fulfill a specific purpose.
layman_explanation: Asking for only your email address to send a newsletter, rather than asking for your phone number and home address.

short_definition: The legal right of individuals to have personal data permanently erased by data controllers.
layman_explanation: Demanding that a social media site completely delete your account and all records of your posts forever.

short_definition: Engineering products to protect user privacy automatically from the beginning of development.
layman_explanation: Designing a smartphone app that keeps your location hidden by default, rather than making you hunt for privacy settings.

short_definition: Irreversibly altering personal data so that the individual cannot be identified by any means.
layman_explanation: Removing names and addresses from customer surveys so researchers see answers without knowing who wrote them.

short_definition: Replacing private identifiers with artificial codes, allowing re-identification only with a separate secret key.
layman_explanation: Replacing patient names with ID numbers like 'Patient #402', while keeping the real name list in a separate safe.

short_definition: The concept that digital data is subject to the privacy laws of the country where it is physically located.
layman_explanation: Data stored in German data centers must obey German privacy laws, regardless of who owns the server.

short_definition: The organization or entity that determines the purposes and means of processing personal data.
layman_explanation: The business that decides why and how customer information is collected.

short_definition: A third-party entity that processes personal data strictly on behalf of a data controller.
layman_explanation: A cloud payroll company that calculates paychecks using employee data provided by an employer.

short_definition: A process to systematically analyze, identify, and minimize data protection risks of a project.
layman_explanation: A risk study conducted before launching a new app to make sure it won't leak user information.

short_definition: Software tools that inform visitors about data collection and collect legally valid consent preferences.
layman_explanation: The pop-up banner on websites asking you to accept or reject cookie tracking.

short_definition: A website notification allowing users to choose which tracking cookies they permit to run in their browser.
layman_explanation: A prompt letting you choose whether a news site can track your browsing habits for targeted ads.

short_definition: A system for sharing information about a dataset by adding mathematical noise to hide individual identities.
layman_explanation: Adding random noise to survey data so scientists see broad trends without identifying any single participant.

short_definition: An organization's established rules defining how long data must be kept and when it must be destroyed.
layman_explanation: A company rule stating 'Delete all customer support chats automatically after 90 days.'

short_definition: A request made by an individual asking an organization for a copy of all personal data held about them.
layman_explanation: Asking a company: 'Send me a file containing every single piece of information you have collected about me.'

short_definition: The right of users to obtain and reuse their personal data across different services easily.
layman_explanation: Clicking a button to download your music playlists from one streaming service and upload them to another.

short_definition: Deceptive user interface designs crafted to trick users into making choices against their privacy interests.
layman_explanation: Making the 'Accept All Cookies' button big and bright, while hiding the 'Reject All' button behind three sub-menus.

short_definition: Transferring personal data across international borders, subject to specific legal frameworks.
layman_explanation: Sending customer records from a server in France to a server in the United States.

short_definition: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard regulating organizations handling major credit cards.
layman_explanation: Security rules that any shop or website must follow if they accept credit card payments.

short_definition: An auditing framework evaluating service organizations on security, availability, processing integrity, and privacy.
layman_explanation: An independent seal of approval proving a cloud service provider handles customer data securely.

short_definition: An international standard specifying requirements for establishing an Information Security Management System (ISMS).
layman_explanation: A globally recognized blueprint for managing corporate information security risks.

short_definition: Categorizing data into sensitivity levels (e.g., Public, Internal, Confidential) to apply appropriate controls.
layman_explanation: Stamping documents as 'Public', 'Confidential', or 'Top Secret' so staff know how to handle them.

short_definition: The overall management of data availability, usability, integrity, and security in an enterprise.
layman_explanation: The master rulebook defining who owns company data, who can see it, and how it must be protected.

short_definition: A legal statement disclosing how an organization gathers, uses, discloses, and manages customer data.
layman_explanation: The public document on a website explaining what data is collected and what the company does with it.

short_definition: Analyzing and monitoring security and privacy risks posed by external vendors and suppliers.
layman_explanation: Checking the security practices of outside contractors before sharing company data with them.

short_definition: An enterprise security leadership role mandated by GDPR to oversee data protection strategy and compliance.
layman_explanation: The designated executive in a company responsible for ensuring user privacy laws are obeyed.

short_definition: Legal mechanisms enabling compliant transatlantic transfers of personal data between the EU and US.
layman_explanation: A legal bridge allowing European customer data to be handled safely by US tech companies.

short_definition: Laws mandating that organizations report data breaches to regulators and affected individuals within specific timeframes.
layman_explanation: Legal rules forcing companies to notify customers within 72 hours if their passwords were leaked.

short_definition: Creating a structurally similar but inauthentic version of data to protect sensitive info in non-production environments.
layman_explanation: Showing only the last four digits of a credit card number on a receipt (e.g., **** **** **** 1234).

short_definition: The right of individuals to have inaccurate or incomplete personal data corrected by an organization.
layman_explanation: Demanding that a credit bureau fix an incorrect home address or wrong name spelling on your file.

short_definition: Requiring a clear, affirmative action from users before collecting or processing their personal data.
layman_explanation: Requiring you to manually check an empty box before sending you promotional text messages.

short_definition: Giving users the ability to declare that they do not want their data collected, used, or sold.
layman_explanation: Clicking an 'Unsubscribe' link at the bottom of an email newsletter to stop receiving messages.

short_definition: A operational model where user data is processed immediately in memory and never saved to persistent storage.
layman_explanation: Processing your voice command in real time and instantly discarding the recording without saving it.

short_definition: Allowing users to disable background collection of software usage data and crash diagnostics.
layman_explanation: Turning off a toggle in settings so an app stops sending usage statistics back to developers.

short_definition: A business model focused on monetizing personal data collected through extensive monitoring of user behavior.
layman_explanation: Offering free apps in exchange for tracking everything you do to sell target ads to advertisers.

short_definition: An individual's right to limit how an organization uses their personal data under certain conditions.
layman_explanation: Telling a company: 'Hold onto my account records for legal reasons, but stop using them for marketing.'

short_definition: Legislation regulating the collection, use, safeguarding, and destruction of biometric identifiers.
layman_explanation: Laws requiring companies to get written permission before collecting your fingerprint or face scan.

short_definition: Creating a comprehensive record of what data an organization holds, where it resides, and who has access.
layman_explanation: Creating a detailed map showing every filing cabinet and server holding customer information.

short_definition: Tech solutions that allow data processing while keeping personal information private and confidential.
layman_explanation: Advanced tools that let analysts search datasets without ever revealing who individuals are.

short_definition: Regulations governing decisions made purely by algorithms without human intervention.
layman_explanation: The right to demand a human review if an AI algorithm automatically denies your loan application.

short_definition: A preliminary questionnaire used to determine if a project collects PII and requires a full DPIA.
layman_explanation: A quick 5-minute survey to check if your project touches user data before starting work.

short_definition: Targeting ads to a consumer based on personal data obtained across distinct websites or applications.
layman_explanation: Seeing an ad for shoes on Instagram right after reading a news article about running shoes on a different site.

short_definition: Browser policies capping how long tracking cookies can remain active on a device before expiring.
layman_explanation: Browsers automatically deleting tracking cookies after 7 days to prevent long-term tracking.

short_definition: The process of deliberately, irreversibly destroying data stored on a memory device.
layman_explanation: Magnetically erasing or physically shredding an old hard drive so data can never be recovered.

short_definition: A public web portal where an organization shares its compliance certifications, security whitepapers, and privacy reports.
layman_explanation: A public page where a tech company posts all its security badges and privacy audit certificates.

short_definition: A audit form sent to software vendors to evaluate their security and privacy compliance posture.
layman_explanation: A detailed security survey you force a supplier to fill out before hiring them.
